name: Parsman IV of Iberia
summary:
P'arsman IV, of the Chosroid Dynasty, was the king (mepe) of Iberia from 406 to 409. A member of the House of Kartli, he succeeded his brother P'arsman III as ruler of the kingdom.

This period marked the beginning of a tumultuous era in Iberian history, characterized by ongoing conflicts with neighboring kingdoms and the rise of Christianity. The Chosroid Dynasty would eventually be overthrown by the Bagratuni Dynasty, which ruled Iberia until its conquest by the Arabs in the 8th century.

P'arsman IV's reign was marked by diplomatic efforts to maintain peace with neighboring kingdoms, including a notable alliance with the Kingdom of Colchis. His death in 409 CE led to a brief power vacuum, which was eventually filled by his son P'arsman V.

The legacy of P'arsman IV can be seen in the continued development of Iberian culture and trade networks, as well as its strategic location along the Silk Road.

The impact of P'arsman IV's reign on Iberian history was significant, but limited to the region. His successor, P'arsman V, would go on to play a crucial role in shaping the future of the kingdom.
